sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:1
items.html:
Seven discernments in the Masach
We already spoke above of the matter of the Masach (in items 62 and 63), and it was explained there that the matter of the Masach is the aspect of the boundary that was made after the Tzimtzum, to receive the light only in the aspect of the first nine Sefirot, and to prevent the light from spreading to the fourth aspect, meaning to Malchut, as in the verse, "hitherto shalt thou come, but no further," etc. And this Masach is a product that results from the Tzimtzum, meaning from the departure of the light. For after the light had departed entirely and completely, meaning from all four aspects that are there, even though the Tzimtzum was only on aspect four alone, as is known, a new form of will was then renewed in the Malchut of Ein Sof, to return and draw the light by the power of the boundary, meaning only from aspect four upward, and not from aspect four downward. And this renewed boundary is called Masach. And since the essence of this boundary rests only on aspect four, which is Malchut, it is therefore discerned that the Masach rests and is established within the vessel of Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:2
items.html:
The boundary and the thickness in the Masach come together as one
Now, there are seven principal discernments to be made here in this Masach. The first discernment is that the aspect of the boundary and the thickness are included and come together as one, without any separation between them whatsoever. For since the boundary that rests in it rests only on the thickness of aspect four alone, as above, it follows that it does not bound and does not prevent the spreading of the light from a degree that does not have the measure of this thickness. Thus the thickness and the boundary come together as one, and both together are called by the name Masach. And it is quite impossible to speak of and discern the Masach by itself, meaning at a time when it is not included in thickness, for then it does not exist at all, so that there would be anything to discern in it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:3
items.html:
There is thickness without a Masach, but there is no Masach without thickness
Indeed, in the vessel of Malchut by itself there is much to discern, meaning at a time when it is not established with a Masach. And first of all one must know that the Malchut of Igulim is not established with a Masach at all, for there is no Masach except in the Sefirot of Yosher. And this has already been explained in Part Two. And there are additional discernments in abundance that will be explained in their place. And when we speak of Malchut alone, the meaning is that we speak only of thickness alone, without the correction of the Masach. Thus a Masach without thickness is impossible, but there is a possibility of thickness without a Masach.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:4
items.html:
The power of prevention in the Masach of the Rosh is in potential, and not in actuality
The second discernment is the aspect of prevention "in potential" within the Masach. For in the matter of the Masach's prevention of the upper light there is a "potential" and an "actual," and this is the difference between Rosh and Guf. And although we say that the upper light spreads until it strikes the Masach that is in the vessel of Malchut, and the Masach returns the light backward, and this returned light clothes upon the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, all this is only in the aspect of potential and not actual in fact, as written above in item 16. Therefore know that all the boundary and prevention upon the light that exists in the Masach that is in the Malchut of the Rosh is only the aspect of prevention in potential, and not in actuality.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:5
items.html:
The power of prevention in the Masach in the aspect of potential is called Peh, and in the aspect of actual is called Tabur
The third discernment is the aspect of prevention in actuality that exists in the Masach. For that clothing and that prevention that occur in the Rosh in the aspect of "potential," as above, come and are revealed in the Guf in actuality. For the Malchut of the Rosh spreads from herself and within herself into ten Sefirot from above downward, which are called collectively by the name Guf, and the Malchut of those ten Sefirot is called by the name Tabur, where all the power of prevention upon the upper light that exists in the Masach of the Rosh is revealed, which does not allow the upper light to clothe except from the Tabur upward, and prevents it from clothing from the Tabur downward. And know that these two names, Peh and Tabur, correspond to these two discernments stated, for the aspect of prevention in potential, of the Masach, is designated by the name Peh, and the aspect of prevention in actuality that exists in the Masach is designated by the name Tabur.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:6
items.html:
The inclusion of the Masach in the first three aspects through its refinement
The fourth discernment is the aspect of the inclusion of the Masach in the thickness of the first three aspects, which comes from the refinement of the Masach mentioned above (in item 4), which occurs through the striking and clashing of Ohr Pnimi and Ohr Makif with one another, as the Rav says (in Chapter One, item 3). And this matter must be well understood, for it is the peg upon which all the wisdom hangs.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:7
items.html:
The inclusion of the Masach in the first three aspects means: the first three aspects of aspect four
And we have already elaborated on this matter in Ohr Pnimi, and there is no room to expand on it here. However, it is necessary to understand here in our matter that this inclusion stated regarding the Masach does not mean that the first three aspects themselves are now contracted, as aspect four was contracted before, but rather all this refinement occurs only in aspect four itself. For it has already been explained in Part Two, in Histaklut Pnimit, that aspect four itself is included of four aspects, from its coming from Ein Sof, blessed be He, may His name be blessed. And therefore the Masach established in it is also included of all four aspects, as above (in item 80), so that all the thickness that is in Malchut is found included in the Masach. And by this you will understand, when it is said that the Masach ascended to Zeir Anpin, to aspect three, the meaning is that aspect four of aspect four was refined of the Masach, and there remained in it only the measure of thickness of aspect three of aspect four, and it is thereby found that its form became equal to the aspect of Zeir Anpin. And know that equivalence of form is unification in the spiritual, and therefore this is called that it ascended and united with Zeir Anpin, as though it were itself the aspect of Zeir Anpin, since there is nothing by which to discern between them. And this is called that it became included with Zeir Anpin. And in this manner you will understand the rest of the inclusions stated regarding the Masach, until it ascended and became included in the Peh of the Rosh, meaning that its form became equal to the aspect of the Masach in potential, and it is not discernible at all that it is of the aspect of the Masach in actuality. And understand this very, very well.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:8
items.html:
If the Masach departs from the vessel, the light departs from it
The fifth discernment is the matter of the cessation of the Masach's action from the vessel, due to its departure from there. That is, at the time the Masach is refined from aspect four to aspect three, at which point the Masach is discerned to have left the vessel of Malchut and ascended to the vessel of Zeir Anpin. Now, seemingly, Malchut has been freed from the power of prevention and boundary that had rested upon her, and henceforth she can receive the upper light without hindrance. However, this is not so; on the contrary, she remains in complete darkness, due to the departure of the Masach from her. And this is for the reason that from the first Tzimtzum onward, Malchut is no longer fit to receive any light at all except through the Masach, in such a way that both actions—both the receiving of the light and the rejection of the light—are bound up with the Masach. For just as it rejects the light from the last aspect, so it binds and clothes the lights that are from it and above. And understand this well.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:9
items.html:
The Masach that receives the thickness of the Rosh anew after its refinement
The sixth discernment is the thickness of the Rosh acquired anew by the Masach after its refinement. This is through its ascent and arrival to the Malchut of the Rosh, and there it becomes included, as written at length (in Chapter Four, item 50, and in Ohr Pnimi). See there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 5:10
items.html:
The Masach that receives the thickness of the Guf after its refinement
The seventh discernment is the thickness of the Guf acquired anew by the Masach after its refinement, as written there in Ohr Pnimi, that after it has received from the Masach of the Rosh the thickness that goes from below upward, then all the marks it had absorbed on its way through the Sefirot of the Guf, at the time of its ascent to the Ma'atzil, are aroused in the Masach of the Guf, and these marks are of the aspect of thickness that goes from above downward, meaning of the aspect of Guf. It is thus found that this thickness, which they receive from the Rosh in the aspect of from below upward, is transformed by the marks of the Guf into thickness that goes from above downward, as written in the aforementioned Ohr Pnimi.
